old: The setting fixes one reply (the action) per user turn, but it defines no episode. Chat is usually run as a multi-turn conversation: context carries over and each reply is a new decision. If the episode is a turn, there is exactly one action (yes). If the episode is a conversation, there are many (no). Two other settings point the same way. D-AGENT-A treats a human turn between actions as inside one episode, so a user turn in chat does not by itself end an episode. T-CHAT does use prompt to reply as the episode, which is a bandit. Deployment has no reward or reset to mark an episode, so the turn-level reading is a modelling choice, not a fact of the setting. The cell for action in D-CHAT says 'One reply per turn', so it supports the per-turn count only. D-RL is not the model here: there the episode is explicit, with many actions per episode.
new: The episode is one conversation (cell episode, D-CHAT), and each user turn gets its own reply, so an episode has many actions.
